title: Pezeshkian Pledges Full Government Support to Modernize Iran's Armed Forces
detail: President Masoud Pezeshkian met with Army Commander-in-Chief Major General Amir Hatami in Tehran. Pezeshkian stated the government would deploy 'all available capacities' to modernize and strengthen Iran's Armed Forces, praising their 'decisive, intelligent, and deterrent' responses to US-Israeli attacks during the June 2025 conflict. General Hatami reported the Army is 'fully prepared to deliver a decisive, regret-inducing response' to any future aggression. The meeting signaled the Pezeshkian government's alignment with the military establishment despite the reformist president's stated preference for diplomacy — reflecting the constraints of Iran's post-war political dynamics where the Supreme Leader and IRGC retain ultimate authority over defense policy.

media.caption: President Pezeshkian meets Army chief Hatami and pledges full government support for Iran's military modernization

title: Iran Secretly Executes Four Including Kurdish Political Activists Without Family Notification
detail: Amnesty International and Euronews reported that Iran secretly executed four men — including two Kurdish political activists identified as Ramin Zale and Karim Maroufpour at Naqadeh Prison, and two Iraqi nationals convicted on espionage charges — without notifying their families in advance. The executions brought Iran's 2026 total to over 200 in fewer than five months, continuing at a rate Amnesty attributed in part to wartime political repression. Iran's record of 2,159 executions in 2025 — the highest since 1981 — had already drawn UN condemnation. Amnesty documented that the Kurdish activists were convicted under vague national security charges in trials that lacked basic due process guarantees, with convictions based partly on confessions obtained under duress.

media.caption: Iran secretly executes four men including Kurdish political activists without notifying their families

title: Rubio Sees "Some Good Signs" for Iran Peace Deal; Warns Hormuz Tolls Are Dealbreaker
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told the Financial Times there were 'some good signs' that an agreement with Iran may be reached, in the most optimistic public US assessment of the negotiations to date. Iran's Foreign Ministry responded that the latest US proposal 'reduced the gaps to some extent.' Global stock markets rose on the positive signals, with oil prices edging lower on expectations of potential Hormuz reopening. However, Rubio simultaneously issued a sharp warning: any deal would be 'unfeasible' if Iran pursued transit tolls on Strait of Hormuz shipping — directly rejecting a key Iranian demand that Tehran claimed was a sovereign right over its territorial waters. The mixed signals reflected the narrow and complex path toward a comprehensive settlement.

media.caption: Rubio says Iran peace talks show good signs but warns that Hormuz toll demands would make deal unfeasible
